The text is complete and faithful, except that 'Moses schreibet' comes out as the garbled 'Mosesreibet' and 'darnach' has a stray letter.

This is a close, complete transcription of both columns and the marginal notes, but it has a few word misreads: 'deß' where the page has 'deñ' (denn), 'versehen' where it has 'versetzen', and an inserted 'sie'.

Half a line is missing in the first paragraph ('abgeschnitten … Was be-'), so the sentence about the higher triad makes no sense; the rest is faithful.

The text matches the page wherever the page can be read, but in the second paragraph the transcription quietly supplies about a dozen line-endings that are cut off in the scan, and in one place it gives "den Ton" where the page has "diesen Ton".

The text beside the image belongs to the previous page (102). The image shows p. 103, 'Vom Vortrage', with §§ 2–4 on good delivery (Stärcke, Schwäche, Druck…), and none of that text is in the transcription.

The two handwritten captions don't match the plate: the upper one has words the scribe didn't write, the lower one drops 'den', and the picture description misstates the action.

The text is complete and accurate apart from one misread word, 'fuyant' where the page has 'suyuant', and a few spellings changed to modern forms such as 'tambourin'.
The page image is cropped on the right, but the transcription quietly fills in the cut-off line endings. It also turns 'ÉCONOMISME' into 'ÉCONOMIE' and 'Art. II' into 'art. 11'.
